questions.question: In its 2010 Advisory Opinion regarding Kosovo, what key legal finding did the International Court of Justice (ICJ) make regarding general international law?
options: General international law contains no applicable prohibition against unilateral declarations of independence.
Unilateral declarations of independence are inherently illegal unless sanctioned by a binding UN Security Council resolution.
The legal principle of territorial integrity applies directly to prohibit sub-state actors from declaring independence.
Unilateral declarations of independence automatically confer statehood under international law regardless of third-State recognition.

questions.question: Under Article 77 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), what is the legal character of a coastal State's sovereign rights over its continental shelf?
options: They must be formally claimed through periodic notification to the International Seabed Authority.
They are exclusive and do not depend on occupation or any express proclamation.
They apply only up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline, beyond which all rights are lost.
They confer full territorial sovereignty, equivalent in scope to a State's land territory.

questions.question: Under Article 1 of the 1933 Montevideo Convention on the Rights and Duties of States, which of the following is NOT one of the four traditional criteria for statehood?
options: A permanent population
A defined territory
Formal recognition by a majority of UN member states
Capacity to enter into relations with other states

questions.question: Under Article 33(2) of the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, a contracting State may exceptionally refuse non-refoulement protection to a refugee under which of the following conditions?
options: The host State is experiencing a severe national economic downturn caused by severe population influx.
The refugee entered the territory of the host State without a valid passport or visa.
The origin State provides diplomatic assurances that the refugee will not face economic hardship upon return.
There are reasonable grounds for regarding the refugee as a danger to the security of the host country.

questions.question: In the formation of customary international law, how is the subjective element of 'opinio juris sive necessitatis' defined?
options: The conviction held by States that a practice is rendered obligatory by the existence of a rule of law.
The physical repetition of uniform State conduct over a prolonged period of time.
The formal consent expressed by States during treaty negotiations prior to signature.
The general compliance of non-State actors with international soft law instruments.
